instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Drive my running app through some steps and report what is actually on the screen after each: which controls exist, what a click would land on, errors, timing", and give it app_url (The address of the running app: http, https, file or data.); steps.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-what-a-running-app-shows and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer, does each step's `do` (the same actions as a walk: goto, click, fill, press, upload, wait, on a control named by role and name), then reads what the page holds as the step's `observe` asks: `elements` (for each match of a selector: its box, cursor, stacking, opacity, whether it is disabled, what a pointer aimed at its own centre would land on, and `pointer_is_self`, which tells a control that is missing from one a layer covers), `count`, `attributes` (named attributes and the form value), `text`, `global_path` (whether a dotted name exists on the page and its kind) and `media_ready` (milliseconds until a video or audio can play).
